title: 02 — Create the project inside the Organization
html:
English | Português (Brasil)

02 — Create the project inside the Organization

With the Organization created, the operator creates the MeuApp workspace — the scheduling product. A product workspace is the unit where the workflow happens: requirements live in it, specs descend into it, delivery moves in it. The full concept: docs/concepts/organization.md.

The wizard again — now inside the org

cd MinhaOrganizacao
golmet init

The wizard opens again, but with a difference: since the current directory is an Organization, the second option comes alive:

◆ What do you want to initialize? (↑/↓ move · enter confirms · esc cancels)

    Organization the root that groups the workspaces
>   Product workspace inside an existing Organization new project inside the root
    Free-root product workspace independent new project

The cursor is now on option 2 (the last used), and the wizard knows the root is an Organization — The operator confirms with enter.

◆ Choose the Organization (↑/↓ move · enter confirms · esc cancels)

  1. MinhaOrganizacao — C:\company\MinhaOrganizacao
  2. Outra — manual path — the Organization is not in the catalog

The list comes from the global catalog — the org he created in tutorial 01 is already there. Enter on MinhaOrganizacao. The wizard asks for the product name: MeuApp. Summary, ENTER, created:

product MeuApp initialized at C:\company\MinhaOrganizacao\MeuApp — 9 created, 0 skipped
container updated: products: [MeuApp]
organization versioning model: org-repo
product WITHOUT its own .golmet/ — the kit zone is the organization's (org-repo)

Three lines worth reading. The products: [MeuApp] is the org recognizing its child. The "versioning model: org-repo" says the ORG is the repository — MeuApp is a folder versioned inside it, with no .gitignore of its own. And the product was born without its own kit zone: the .golmet/ zone is the organization's, shared — the full concept in docs/concepts/layers.md.

What was born in MeuApp — and each document's role

Five documents and three folders. Each one is a character in the story coming ahead (the full artifact map is in docs/concepts/artefatos.md):

  • golmet.yaml — the workspace manifest. The kit reads from here that this is a workspace (not an org) and that the format is 1.
  • PROJECT_CHARTER.md — the charter: what the product IS. Name, owner, purpose, the code repositories. It is the seed of everything that comes after — the charter is the first document of the DAG, and all the others descend from it one way or another.
  • REQUIREMENTS.md — the business rules document. Born empty, it is the one that grows the most: each requirement becomes a ## RN-001 — title section with state (draft → confirmed → active) and evidence. The client validates here.
  • CHANGE_REQUESTS.md and DECISIONS.md — where scope changes and technical decisions get recorded. They exist as their own documents because they are the records the team will re-read when someone asks "why?".
  • reverse/CANDIDATES.md — the candidate knowledge queue (in brownfield projects, what was discovered from legacy code enters here).
  • specs/ and delivery/ (folders created) — where the technical analysis descends and where features move, respectively.
  • golmet.index.json — the state index baseline: the validation machine compares the state declared in the documents against this kit-managed cache.

What comes next

The workspace is ready and empty — empty on purpose. Life starts when the AI walks in: 03 — working with AI.
